did_you_know.text: Did you know? In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, he had dreams that troubled him deeply. The text says that his spirit was alarmed and that sleep eluded him.
Did you know? Beginning with verse 4, the chapter contains an extensive section in Aramaic. The Chaldeans address the king in Aramaic and ask him to tell them the dream so they can interpret it.

Did you know? Nebuchadnezzar demanded that the wise men of Babylon not only interpret the dream but also reveal what the dream itself had been. If they failed, he threatened to have them killed and their houses destroyed.
Did you know? Daniel did not act alone. He told Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah—his companions—about the danger and asked them to pray to the God of heaven for the mystery to be revealed.
Did you know? The mystery of the king’s dream was revealed to Daniel in a night vision. Immediately afterward, he blessed the God of heaven and did not take credit for revealing the interpretation.
Did you know? After the mystery was revealed, Daniel asked Arioch not to destroy the wise men of Babylon and offered to bring the king someone who could tell him the interpretation of the dream.

Did you know? The statue in the dream was enormous and terrifying, and it was made of different materials: its head was gold, its chest and arms were silver, its body was bronze, its legs were iron, and its feet were a mixture of iron and clay.
Did you know? A stone cut out without human hands struck the statue’s feet and shattered its parts. Then it became a great mountain that filled the whole earth.

Did you know? According to Daniel’s interpretation, the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed or handed over to another people. Unlike the kingdoms represented by the statue, it will endure forever.

Did you know? After hearing the interpretation, Nebuchadnezzar honored Daniel and acknowledged that his God reveals mysteries. Daniel was appointed ruler over the entire province of Babylon, and his companions were given positions in the administration.
